account: Gutherz, Gordin, Saenz, Levy and Berant (PNAS Nexus, 2 May 2023) trained neural machine translation models to render Akkadian into English. One works directly from cuneiform Unicode glyphs (C2E), one from transliteration (T2E). They report BLEU4 scores of 36.52 and 37.47, improvements of 9.43 and 13.96 over a translation-memory baseline. Results were best on sentences of about 118 characters or fewer. They propose a human-in-the-loop system in which scholars correct outputs. No passage read and accepted by scholars is named. The authors report hallucinations in longer or fragmented texts. The work stands as a capability demonstration. The group's 2020 PLoS ONE paper (Akkademia) reported up to 97% accuracy for automatic transliteration and segmentation.

ai_role.statement: The models' translation quality is reported by their developers in a peer-reviewed paper. No scholar-accepted translation of a specific text is attributed to them. The authors note limits on longer and fragmented texts.

fields.account: Gutherz, Gordin, Saenz, Levy and Berant (PNAS Nexus, 2 May 2023) trained neural machine translation models to render Akkadian into English. One works directly from cuneiform Unicode glyphs (C2E), one from transliteration (T2E). They report BLEU4 scores of 36.52 and 37.47, improvements of 9.43 and 13.96 over a translation-memory baseline. Results were best on sentences of about 118 characters or fewer. They propose a human-in-the-loop system in which scholars correct outputs. No passage read and accepted by scholars is named. The authors report hallucinations in longer or fragmented texts. The work stands as a capability demonstration. The group's 2020 PLoS ONE paper (Akkademia) reported up to 97% accuracy for automatic transliteration and segmentation.
